lessons.title: My, your, his, her: possessives and have

theory.en:
## Possessive adjectives

Possessive adjectives say who something belongs to. They go **before a noun** and never change: *my brother*, *my brothers*.

| Subject pronoun | Possessive adjective | Example |
|---|---|---|
| I | **my** | *This is **my** sister.* |
| you | **your** | *Is that **your** dad?* |
| he | **his** | *Tom is here with **his** son.* |
| she | **her** | *Anna and **her** husband are from Peru.* |
| it | **its** | *The dog is happy. **Its** name is Toby.* |
| we | **our** | *We love **our** grandparents.* |
| they | **their** | *My cousins live with **their** mom.* |

Use **his** for a man or a boy and **her** for a woman or a girl. It depends on the person who has the thing, not on the thing.

### Watch out

- **its** (possessive) ≠ **it's** (*it is*): *It's a dog. Its name is Toby.*
- **their** (possessive) ≠ **they're** (*they are*) ≠ **there** (a place).

## Possessive *'s*

With names and nouns, add **'s** to show who has something:

- *Sara**'s** brother* (the brother of Sara)
- *my dad**'s** car* (the car of my dad)

With plural nouns that end in *-s*, add only the apostrophe: *my parents**'** house*.

## The verb *have*

Use **have** to talk about family, things and how people look.

| Subject | *have* |
|---|---|
| I / you / we / they | **have** |
| he / she / it | **has** |

- *I **have** two brothers.*
- *My sister **has** long hair.*
- *We **have** a dog.*

To ask about family, learn this question as a chunk: *Do you have any brothers or sisters?* — *Yes, I have one sister.* / *No, I don't.* (You will study questions like this in unit 5.)
theory.es:
## Adjetivos posesivos

Los adjetivos posesivos dicen de quién es algo. Van **antes del sustantivo** y nunca cambian: *my brother* (mi hermano), *my brothers* (mis hermanos).

| Pronombre sujeto | Adjetivo posesivo | Ejemplo |
|---|---|---|
| I | **my** (mi, mis) | *This is **my** sister.* (Ella es mi hermana.) |
| you | **your** (tu, tus, su, sus) | *Is that **your** dad?* (¿Ese es tu papá?) |
| he | **his** (su, de él) | *Tom is here with **his** son.* (Tom está aquí con su hijo.) |
| she | **her** (su, de ella) | *Anna and **her** husband are from Peru.* (Anna y su esposo son de Perú.) |
| it | **its** (su, de una cosa o animal) | *The dog is happy. **Its** name is Toby.* (El perro está feliz. Se llama Toby.) |
| we | **our** (nuestro, nuestra) | *We love **our** grandparents.* (Queremos a nuestros abuelos.) |
| they | **their** (su, de ellos) | *My cousins live with **their** mom.* (Mis primos viven con su mamá.) |

En español *su* sirve para todo; en inglés tienes que elegir. Usa **his** si el dueño es un hombre o un niño y **her** si es una mujer o una niña. Depende de la persona que tiene la cosa, no de la cosa.

### Cuidado

- **its** (posesivo) ≠ **it's** (*it is*): *It's a dog. Its name is Toby.*
- **their** (posesivo) ≠ **they're** (*they are*) ≠ **there** (allí).

## El posesivo *'s*

Con nombres y sustantivos, agrega **'s** para decir de quién es algo. El orden es el contrario al español:

- *Sara**'s** brother* (el hermano de Sara)
- *my dad**'s** car* (el carro de mi papá)

Con sustantivos en plural que terminan en *-s*, agrega solo el apóstrofo: *my parents**'** house* (la casa de mis padres).

## El verbo *have*

Usa **have** (tener) para hablar de la familia, de las cosas y de cómo es una persona.

| Sujeto | *have* |
|---|---|
| I / you / we / they | **have** |
| he / she / it | **has** |

- *I **have** two brothers.* (Tengo dos hermanos.)
- *My sister **has** long hair.* (Mi hermana tiene el pelo largo.)
- *We **have** a dog.* (Tenemos un perro.)

Recuerda: la edad no se dice con *have* sino con *be*: *I'm twenty* (tengo veinte años).

Para preguntar por la familia, aprende esta pregunta como un bloque: *Do you have any brothers or sisters?* (¿Tienes hermanos?) — *Yes, I have one sister.* / *No, I don't.* (Estudiarás este tipo de preguntas en la unidad 5.)

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: "This is my brother. ___ name is Leo."

explanation.en: *My brother* is a man (**he**), so we use **his**: *His name is Leo.*
explanation.es: *My brother* es un hombre (**he**), así que usamos **his**: *His name is Leo.*

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Anna and Ben are married. ___ house is in Toronto."

explanation.en: The house belongs to Anna and Ben (**they**), so we use the possessive **their**. *There* is a place and *they're* means *they are*.
explanation.es: La casa es de Anna y Ben (**they**), así que usamos el posesivo **their**. *There* es un lugar y *they're* significa *they are*.

exercises.prompt: Match each subject pronoun with its possessive adjective.

explanation.en: I → *my*, you → *your*, he → *his*, she → *her*, it → *its*, we → *our*, they → *their*.
explanation.es: I → *my*, you → *your*, he → *his*, she → *her*, it → *its*, we → *our*, they → *their*.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a possessive adjective: my, your, his, her, its, our or their.

content.text: We are brothers, and {{g1}} parents are from Peru. Our sister is a nurse, and {{g2}} hospital is in Lima. Our cousins live with {{g3}} grandmother.

explanation.en: *We* → **our**; *our sister* is a woman → **her**; *our cousins* are many people (*they*) → **their**.
explanation.es: *We* → **our**; *our sister* es una mujer → **her**; *our cousins* son varias personas (*they*) → **their**.

exercises.prompt: "The car of my father" — choose the natural English.

explanation.en: Put the person first and add **'s**: *my father's car*. Don't forget the apostrophe (').
explanation.es: Pon primero a la persona y agrega **'s**: *my father's car*. No olvides el apóstrofo (').

exercises.prompt: Complete with have or has.

content.text: I {{g1}} two sisters. My brother {{g2}} a dog. We {{g3}} a big family.

explanation.en: *I* and *we* take **have**; *my brother* (*he*) takes **has**.
explanation.es: *I* y *we* llevan **have**; *my brother* (*he*) lleva **has**.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

explanation.en: Owner + **'s** + noun, then the verb: *Sara's brother has blue eyes.*
explanation.es: Dueño + **'s** + sustantivo, luego el verbo: *Sara's brother has blue eyes.*

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

explanation.en: The possessive goes before the noun: *Our grandparents* (*they*) take **have**.
explanation.es: El posesivo va antes del sustantivo: *Our grandparents* (*they*) lleva **have**.

exercises.prompt: Say the same thing. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: This is the bike of Paul.

explanation.en: *The bike of Paul* sounds unnatural in English. Say *Paul's bike*.
explanation.es: *The bike of Paul* no suena natural en inglés. Se dice *Paul's bike*.

exercises.prompt: Make one sentence. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: She has a brother. He is Tom.

explanation.en: The brother belongs to *she*, so we say **her** brother: *Her brother is Tom.*
explanation.es: El hermano es de *she* (ella), así que decimos **her** brother: *Her brother is Tom.*

exercises.prompt: Complete with its or it's.

content.text: We have a dog, and {{g1}} name is Max. I think {{g2}} a very nice dog.

explanation.en: **its** + noun is possessive (*its name*); **it's** means *it is* (*it's a nice dog*).
explanation.es: **its** + sustantivo es posesivo (*its name*); **it's** significa *it is* (*it's a nice dog*).

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Mark ___ two brothers."

explanation.en: *Mark* is one person (**he**), so we use **has**. *Is* doesn't mean *tener*.
explanation.es: *Mark* es una persona (**he**), así que usamos **has**. *Is* no significa tener.

theory.en:
## Family

| Man / boy | Woman / girl | Both |
|---|---|---|
| father (*dad*) | mother (*mom*) | parents |
| brother | sister | — |
| son | daughter | children |
| husband | wife | — |
| grandfather | grandmother | grandparents |
| uncle | aunt | — |
| — | — | cousin |

- *Mom* and *dad* are informal; we use them a lot when we talk to or about our parents.
- **Parents** means your mother and your father, not all your family.
- **Cousin** is the same word for a boy or a girl.
- The plural of *child* is **children**.
- A **friend** is not family, but a person you like and know well.

## Describing people

Use **be** for height and age, and **have** for hair and eyes:

| *be* | *have* |
|---|---|
| *He's **tall**.* / *She's **short**.* | *She **has** long hair.* / *He **has** short hair.* |
| *She's **young**.* / *He's **old**.* | *He **has** blue eyes.* / *She **has** brown eyes.* |

With hair, the length comes before the color: *She has **long dark** hair.* *He has **short blond** hair.*

It's more polite to say *He's **not very tall*** than *He's short*.
theory.es:
## La familia

| Hombre / niño | Mujer / niña | Los dos |
|---|---|---|
| father (padre, *dad* papá) | mother (madre, *mom* mamá) | parents (padres) |
| brother (hermano) | sister (hermana) | — |
| son (hijo) | daughter (hija) | children (hijos) |
| husband (esposo) | wife (esposa) | — |
| grandfather (abuelo) | grandmother (abuela) | grandparents (abuelos) |
| uncle (tío) | aunt (tía) | — |
| — | — | cousin (primo, prima) |

- *Mom* y *dad* son informales; los usamos mucho para hablar con o sobre nuestros padres.
- **Parents** significa tu madre y tu padre, no toda tu familia (falso amigo: *parientes* es *relatives*).
- **Cousin** es la misma palabra para primo y prima.
- El plural de *child* (niño, hijo) es **children**.
- Un **friend** (amigo, amiga) no es familia, sino una persona que te cae bien y conoces.

## Describir a una persona

Usa **be** para la estatura y la edad, y **have** para el pelo y los ojos:

| *be* | *have* |
|---|---|
| *He's **tall**.* (Es alto.) / *She's **short**.* (Es baja.) | *She **has** long hair.* (Tiene el pelo largo.) / *He **has** short hair.* (Tiene el pelo corto.) |
| *She's **young**.* (Es joven.) / *He's **old**.* (Es mayor.) | *He **has** blue eyes.* (Tiene los ojos azules.) / *She **has** brown eyes.* (Tiene los ojos cafés.) |

Con el pelo, el largo va antes del color y los dos van antes de *hair*: *She has **long dark** hair.* (Tiene el pelo largo y oscuro.) *He has **short blond** hair.* (Tiene el pelo corto y rubio.)

Es más amable decir *He's **not very tall*** (no es muy alto) que *He's short*.

exercises.prompt: Match each man with the woman in the same position.

explanation.en: father – mother, brother – sister, son – daughter, husband – wife, uncle – aunt, grandfather – grandmother.
explanation.es: father – mother (padre – madre), brother – sister (hermano – hermana), son – daughter (hijo – hija), husband – wife (esposo – esposa), uncle – aunt (tío – tía), grandfather – grandmother (abuelo – abuela).

exercises.prompt: Your mother's sister is your ___.

explanation.en: The sister of your mother or father is your **aunt**.
explanation.es: La hermana de tu madre o de tu padre es tu **aunt** (tía).

exercises.prompt: Your uncle's son is your ___.

explanation.en: The child of your aunt or uncle is your **cousin**, for a boy or a girl.
explanation.es: El hijo o la hija de tu tío o tu tía es tu **cousin** (primo o prima).

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its Spanish meaning.

explanation.en: Careful with **parents**: it means your mother and father only, not all your relatives.
explanation.es: Cuidado con **parents**: significa solo tu madre y tu padre, no todos tus parientes.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a family word.

content.text: Your mother's mother is your {{g1}}. Your aunt's son and daughter are your {{g2}}. Your mother and father are your {{g3}}.

explanation.en: Your mother's mother is your **grandmother**; your aunt's children are your **cousins** (plural); your mother and father are your **parents**.
explanation.es: La madre de tu madre es tu **grandmother** (abuela); los hijos de tu tía son tus **cousins** (primos, en plural); tu madre y tu padre son tus **parents** (padres).

exercises.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "tall"?

explanation.en: The opposite of *tall* is **short**. The opposite of *young* is *old*.
explanation.es: Lo contrario de *tall* (alto) es **short** (bajo). Lo contrario de *young* (joven) es *old* (mayor).

exercises.prompt: Complete with young or old.

content.text: My grandfather is eighty-five. He's {{g1}}. My baby cousin is one. She's very {{g2}}.

explanation.en: A person with many years is **old**; a person with few years is **young**.
explanation.es: Una persona con muchos años es **old** (mayor); una persona con pocos años es **young** (joven).

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct order: "She has ___."

explanation.en: Adjectives go before the noun, and length comes before color: *long dark hair*.
explanation.es: Los adjetivos van antes del sustantivo, y el largo va antes del color: *long dark hair*.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

explanation.en: *Have* for hair, then length + color + *hair*: *He has short blond hair.*
explanation.es: *Have* para el pelo, luego largo + color + *hair*: *He has short blond hair.*

exercises.prompt: Say the same thing. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: Ana is the daughter of my uncle.

explanation.en: The daughter of your uncle is your **cousin**: *Ana is my cousin.*
explanation.es: La hija de tu tío es tu **cousin** (prima): *Ana is my cousin.*

exercises.prompt: Lisa and Paul are married. Paul is Lisa's ___.

explanation.en: Paul is a man married to Lisa, so he is her **husband**. Lisa is Paul's *wife*.
explanation.es: Paul es un hombre casado con Lisa, así que es su **husband** (esposo). Lisa es la *wife* (esposa) de Paul.

exercises.prompt: Complete the description.

content.text: My friend Leo has green {{g1}} and long dark {{g2}}. He isn't short. He's very {{g3}}.

explanation.en: Green goes with **eyes**, long dark with **hair**, and the opposite of *short* is **tall**.
explanation.es: Green (verdes) va con **eyes** (ojos), long dark (largo y oscuro) con **hair** (pelo), y lo contrario de *short* es **tall** (alto).

theory.en:
## Listening: talking about a photo

When people show a photo, they use a few phrases again and again:

| To ask | To answer |
|---|---|
| *Who's that?* / *Who's the tall man?* | *That's my dad.* |
| *Who are they?* | *These are my sisters.* |
| *Is your uncle in the photo?* | *No, he isn't.* |
| *Where are you?* | *I'm here, with my grandfather.* |

- **This / these** point at people or things near you; **that** points at something farther away.
- *The man **with** the beard* / *the boy **with** the dog*: **with** helps you know which person.

### Tips

- Before you listen, read the questions: they tell you what to listen for (a name, an age, a color).
- The first time, listen for **who** the people are. The second time, listen for details.
- Don't worry if you don't understand every word.

### Dictation

In a dictation you hear a sentence and write it. Listen once for the meaning, then again to write each word. Check capital letters, apostrophes (*Max's*) and the final period.
theory.es:
## Comprensión auditiva: hablar de una foto

Cuando alguien muestra una foto, usa algunas frases una y otra vez:

| Para preguntar | Para responder |
|---|---|
| *Who's that?* (¿Quién es?) / *Who's the tall man?* (¿Quién es el hombre alto?) | *That's my dad.* (Es mi papá.) |
| *Who are they?* (¿Quiénes son?) | *These are my sisters.* (Estas son mis hermanas.) |
| *Is your uncle in the photo?* (¿Tu tío está en la foto?) | *No, he isn't.* |
| *Where are you?* (¿Dónde estás tú?) | *I'm here, with my grandfather.* (Aquí, con mi abuelo.) |

- **This / these** señalan personas o cosas cerca de ti; **that** señala algo más lejos.
- *The man **with** the beard* (el hombre de barba) / *the boy **with** the dog* (el niño con el perro): **with** te ayuda a saber de qué persona se habla.

### Consejos

- Antes de escuchar, lee las preguntas: te dicen qué tienes que buscar (un nombre, una edad, un color).
- La primera vez, escucha **quiénes** son las personas. La segunda vez, escucha los detalles.
- No te preocupes si no entiendes todas las palabras.

### Dictado

En un dictado escuchas una oración y la escribes. Escucha una vez para entender el significado y otra vez para escribir cada palabra. Revisa las mayúsculas, los apóstrofos (*Max's*) y el punto final.

exercises.prompt: Listen. The photo is from whose birthday?

explanation.en: Daniel says: *It's from my grandmother's birthday. She's eighty in the photo!*
explanation.es: Daniel dice: *It's from my grandmother's birthday. She's eighty in the photo!* (Es del cumpleaños de mi abuela. ¡Tiene ochenta en la foto!)

exercises.prompt: Who is Robert?

explanation.en: *That's my dad. His name is Robert.* He's the tall man with the beard.
explanation.es: *That's my dad. His name is Robert.* (Es mi papá. Se llama Robert.) Es el hombre alto de barba.

exercises.prompt: Match each person with the description.

right.text: short blond hair and blue eyes
a little boy with a dog

explanation.en: Robert is *the tall man with the beard*, Carmen *has beautiful long hair* and is from Chile, Lily *has short blond hair and blue eyes*, and Max is *the little boy with the dog*. Nobody is described as short with dark hair.
explanation.es: Robert es *the tall man with the beard*, Carmen *has beautiful long hair* y es de Chile, Lily *has short blond hair and blue eyes*, y Max es *the little boy with the dog*. Nadie se describe como bajo y de pelo oscuro.

exercises.prompt: Which two sentences are true? Choose two.

explanation.en: *He's a doctor* (Robert) and Uncle Tom is *the photographer*. Daniel has two **sisters**, and Lily is fifteen; Sofia is twenty-two.
explanation.es: *He's a doctor* (Robert) y el tío Tom es *the photographer* (el fotógrafo). Daniel tiene dos **hermanas**, y Lily tiene quince; Sofia tiene veintidós.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the sentence.

explanation.en: *My mom is from Chile.* *Mom* is informal for *mother*, and countries start with a capital letter.
explanation.es: *My mom is from Chile.* *Mom* es la forma informal de *mother*, y los países empiezan con mayúscula.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the sisters' ages.

explanation.en: Daniel says: *Sofia is twenty-two and Lily is fifteen.*
explanation.es: Daniel dice: *Sofia is twenty-two and Lily is fifteen.* (Sofia tiene veintidós y Lily quince.)

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the sentence.

solution.transcript: Lily has short blond hair and blue eyes.

explanation.en: *Lily has short blond hair and blue eyes.* *She* takes **has**, and the adjectives go before *hair* and *eyes*.
explanation.es: *Lily has short blond hair and blue eyes.* *She* lleva **has**, y los adjetivos van antes de *hair* y *eyes*.

exercises.prompt: Match each person with who they are.

explanation.en: *That's my cousin Max. He's my uncle Tom's son*, so Tom is Max's dad. Carmen is Daniel's mom, Sofia is his sister and Toby is Max's dog.
explanation.es: *That's my cousin Max. He's my uncle Tom's son* (Es mi primo Max. Es el hijo de mi tío Tom), así que Tom es el papá de Max. Carmen es la mamá de Daniel, Sofia es su hermana y Toby es el perro de Max.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a possessive adjective.

content.text: Daniel's dad is a doctor, and {{g1}} name is Robert. Max has a dog, and {{g2}} name is Toby. Daniel and his grandfather have the same eyes: {{g3}} eyes are green.

explanation.en: The dad is a man → **his**; the dog is an animal → **its**; Daniel and his grandfather are two people (*they*) → **their**.
explanation.es: El papá es un hombre → **his**; el perro es un animal → **its**; Daniel y su abuelo son dos personas (*they*) → **their**.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a true sentence about the conversation.

explanation.en: *Daniel's uncle is the photographer.* That's why he isn't in the photo.
explanation.es: *Daniel's uncle is the photographer.* (El tío de Daniel es el fotógrafo.) Por eso no está en la foto.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the sentence.

solution.transcript: We have the same green eyes.

explanation.en: *We have the same green eyes.* *We* takes **have**, not *has*.
explanation.es: *We have the same green eyes.* (Tenemos los mismos ojos verdes.) *We* lleva **have**, no *has*.

exercises.prompt: Where is Daniel in the photo?

explanation.en: Daniel says: *I'm here, with my grandfather.* The person who isn't in the photo is Uncle Tom.
explanation.es: Daniel dice: *I'm here, with my grandfather.* (Estoy aquí, con mi abuelo.) El que no está en la foto es el tío Tom.

theory.en:
## Writing about your family

A short description of your family has three parts:

1. **Start:** say how big your family is. *I have a small family.* / *There are five people in my family.*
2. **Middle:** one or two sentences about each person: name, age, job, how they look.
3. **End:** a short final sentence. *I love my family!*

### Useful sentences

| To say | Example |
|---|---|
| who | *My mom's name is Carmen.* / *I have two sisters.* |
| age | *She's forty-eight.* (with *be*, not *have*) |
| job | *He's a doctor.* |
| looks | *He's tall. He has short dark hair.* |

### Joining ideas

- **and** adds information: *I have one brother **and** two sisters.*
- **but** shows a difference: *My sister is tall, **but** I'm short.*

### Check your writing

- Names start with a capital letter, and so does **I**.
- *he/she* + **has**; *I/we/they* + **have**.
- *his* for a man, *her* for a woman.
- Every sentence ends with a period (.).

### Model

*I have a small family. My dad's name is Luis. He's fifty and he's a taxi driver. He's tall and he has short gray hair. My mom, Rosa, is a nurse. She has long dark hair and brown eyes. I have one sister, Paula. She's twelve. I love my family!*
theory.es:
## Escribir sobre tu familia

Una descripción corta de tu familia tiene tres partes:

1. **Inicio:** di cómo es tu familia. *I have a small family.* (Tengo una familia pequeña.) / *There are five people in my family.* (En mi familia somos cinco.)
2. **Desarrollo:** una o dos oraciones sobre cada persona: nombre, edad, trabajo, cómo es.
3. **Final:** una oración corta para cerrar. *I love my family!* (¡Quiero a mi familia!)

### Oraciones útiles

| Para decir | Ejemplo |
|---|---|
| quién | *My mom's name is Carmen.* (Mi mamá se llama Carmen.) / *I have two sisters.* |
| edad | *She's forty-eight.* (con *be*, no con *have*) |
| trabajo | *He's a doctor.* (Es médico; en inglés lleva *a*.) |
| aspecto | *He's tall. He has short dark hair.* |

### Unir ideas

- **and** (y) agrega información: *I have one brother **and** two sisters.*
- **but** (pero) muestra una diferencia: *My sister is tall, **but** I'm short.*

### Revisa tu texto

- Los nombres empiezan con mayúscula, y también **I** (yo).
- *he/she* + **has**; *I/we/they* + **have**.
- *his* si es un hombre, *her* si es una mujer.
- Cada oración termina con punto (.).

### Modelo

*I have a small family. My dad's name is Luis. He's fifty and he's a taxi driver. He's tall and he has short gray hair. My mom, Rosa, is a nurse. She has long dark hair and brown eyes. I have one sister, Paula. She's twelve. I love my family!*

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: "This is Sofia. ___ my sister."

explanation.en: The sentence needs a subject and a verb: *She's* = *she is*. *Her* and *his* must go before a noun.
explanation.es: La oración necesita sujeto y verbo: *She's* = *she is*. *Her* y *his* tienen que ir antes de un sustantivo.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

options.text: My brother is twenty years old.

explanation.en: In English, age uses **be**: *My brother is twenty (years old).*
explanation.es: En inglés la edad se dice con **be**, no con *have*: *My brother is twenty (years old).*

exercises.prompt: Match each question with its answer.

left.text: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

explanation.en: *Brothers or sisters* → *I have one sister*; *mom's name* → *her name*; *how old* → an age with *be*; *who* → a person; *what color* → a color.
explanation.es: *Brothers or sisters* → *I have one sister*; *mom's name* → *her name*; *how old* → una edad con *be*; *who* → una persona; *what color* → un color.

exercises.prompt: Complete the text.

content.text: My name {{g1}} Ana. I {{g2}} two brothers, and {{g3}} names are Leo and Max.

explanation.en: *My name **is***; *I **have*** for family; the names belong to the brothers (*they*) → **their**.
explanation.es: *My name **is***; *I **have*** para la familia; los nombres son de los hermanos (*they*) → **their**.

exercises.prompt: Complete with one word.

content.text: Lily is my {{g1}}: she's my uncle's daughter. My grandparents {{g2}} a house in Chile.

explanation.en: Your uncle's daughter is your **cousin**. *My grandparents* (*they*) takes **have**.
explanation.es: La hija de tu tío es tu **cousin** (prima). *My grandparents* (*they*) lleva **have**.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.

explanation.en: *My mother's name* is the subject (the name of my mother), then *is*: *My mother's name is Carmen.*
explanation.es: *My mother's name* (el nombre de mi madre) es el sujeto, luego *is*: *My mother's name is Carmen.*

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.

explanation.en: In questions with *be*, the verb comes first: *Is your brother tall?*
explanation.es: En las preguntas con *be*, el verbo va primero: *Is your brother tall?*

exercises.prompt: Make one sentence. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: I have a brother. He is Leo.

explanation.en: The brother is yours (*I*), so say **my** brother: *My brother is Leo.*
explanation.es: El hermano es tuyo (*I*), así que di **my** brother: *My brother is Leo.*

exercises.prompt: Say the same thing. Use the word in capitals.

content.sentence: Max is the son of Tom.

explanation.en: Use the possessive **'s**: *the son of Tom* → *Tom's son*.
explanation.es: Usa el posesivo **'s**: *the son of Tom* → *Tom's son*.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best word: "My sister is tall, ___ I'm short."

explanation.en: *Tall* and *short* are different, so we join them with **but**. **And** adds similar information.
explanation.es: *Tall* y *short* son diferentes, así que los unimos con **but** (pero). **And** (y) agrega información parecida.

exercises.prompt: Describe your family.

content.task: Write about your family (or an imaginary family) for a class website. Say how many people there are, and for two or three people write their name, age, job and what they look like. End with a short final sentence.

description.en: I wrote about two or three people, with their name, age, job and what they look like.
description.es: Escribí sobre dos o tres personas, con su nombre, edad, trabajo y cómo son.

description.en: I used have/has, possessives (my, his, her, 's) and be for age correctly.
description.es: Usé bien have/has, los posesivos (my, his, her, 's) y be para la edad.

description.en: My text has a start, a middle and an end, and I joined ideas with and or but.
description.es: Mi texto tiene inicio, desarrollo y final, y uní ideas con and o but.

description.en: Names and I have capital letters, and every sentence ends with a period.
description.es: Los nombres y la palabra I llevan mayúscula, y cada oración termina con punto.

solution.model_answer: There are four people in my family. My dad's name is Luis. He's fifty and he's a taxi driver. He's tall and he has short gray hair. My mom, Rosa, is forty-seven. She's a nurse, and she has long dark hair and brown eyes. I have one sister. Her name is Paula and she's twelve. She's short, but she's very funny. I love my family!

description.es: Dije el nombre, la edad, el país y cómo es mi amigo o amiga.
